examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{有名|ゆうめい}な{詩人|しじん}だ。
この{詩|し}は{日本|にほん}の{詩人|しじん}によって{書|か}かれた。
examples.english: This poem was written by a Japanese poet.

examples.japanese: {若|わか}い{詩人|しじん}が{注目|ちゅうもく}を{集|あつ}めている。
examples.english: A young poet is attracting attention.

examples.japanese: その{詩人|しじん}は{美|うつく}しい{自然|しぜん}の{中|なか}で{多|おお}くの{作品|さくひん}を{書|か}いた。
examples.english: That poet wrote many works amid beautiful nature.

examples.japanese: {詩人|しじん}は{言葉|ことば}を{通|とお}して{世界|せかい}を{表現|ひょうげん}する。{彼|かれ}らの{感性|かんせい}は{時代|じだい}を{超|こ}えて{人々|ひとびと}の{心|こころ}に{響|ひび}く。
examples.english: Poets express the world through words. Their sensibility resonates in people's hearts across generations.

notes:
A person who writes {詩|し} (poetry). Used for both modern and classical poets, Japanese and foreign.

ETYMOLOGY:
Compound of {詩|し} (poetry) + {人|じん} (person).

RELATED LITERARY OCCUPATIONS:
- {作家|さっか}: writer, author (general)
- {小説家|しょうせつか}: novelist
- {歌人|かじん}: waka poet (traditional 31-syllable Japanese poetry)
- {俳人|はいじん}: haiku poet
- {劇作家|げきさっか}: playwright

NOTE ON JAPANESE POETRY TYPES:
{詩|し} specifically refers to modern free verse or Western-style poetry. Traditional Japanese poetry forms have their own terms: {和歌|わか} (waka), {俳句|はいく} (haiku), {短歌|たんか} (tanka). So a {詩人|しじん} is distinct from a {歌人|かじん} or {俳人|はいじん}.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {詩人|しじん}になる: to become a poet
- {有名|ゆうめい}な{詩人|しじん}: a famous poet
